# How TCP Congestion Control Adapts to Changing Bandwidth

## Introduction

TCP congestion control is the set of algorithms a TCP sender uses to infer how much capacity is available in the network and to adjust its sending rate accordingly. The core challenge is that the network is a black box: the sender cannot directly measure the bandwidth of the path, nor can it know how many other flows share the bottleneck. Instead, TCP relies on feedback signals—primarily packet loss and round-trip time (RTT) measurements—to infer whether it is sending too fast or too slowly, and it adjusts its congestion window (cwnd) accordingly.
